newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela pioneering new reform formula - Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela pioneering new reform formula - Matos.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has pioneered a new formula for future structural adjustment programs by combining reforms with benefits for workers, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday.

"I think Venezuela has opened a new path for the way to carry out adjustment programs," Matos told local Union Radio station in an interview from Barcelona where he is attending the Inter-American Development Bank annual meeting.
Matos said a team of International Monetary Fund officials currently in Caracas had understood the government's recent decision to give public sector workers a 75 percent pay rise.

"The IMF understood that there was no way to make such an important structural change without the salary adjustments we've made, which open the way to the political and social stabilization which the macroeconomic program requires," he said.

The recent salary rise for public sector workers and the signing Monday of a historic agreement to reform Venezuela's severance payments system were signs that the government was committed to improving real wages, which have fallen to 30 percent of their 1980 level in real terms, Matos said.
